unit: a test id (class::method with data set) that fails or errors on PHP 8.3
baseline: the PHP 7.4 run of the same tree; a test that also fails there is not attributed

outcomes.TP: a predicted rule (will break or may break) with at least one new failing test attributed to it
outcomes.FP: a predicted rule with no new failing test attributed to it
outcomes.MISS: a new failing test attributed to no predicted rule; the reason the catalog lacked it is written in score.json

attribution: a failing test is attributed to a rule when its failure message or stack matches that rule's pattern below
a null pattern means the change is silent; such a rule is attributed only by tracing the failing assertion to the changed behaviour by hand, and the trace is written in score.json
a test that matches no pattern and cannot be traced to a predicted rule is a MISS
a deprecation, warning or risky result that PHPUnit reports without failing the run is not a failure; it is listed in score.json as emitted-only and does not make a TP

patterns.php-8-non-numeric-typeerror: Unsupported operand types: string|A non-numeric value encountered|Unsupported operand types

install: old stack: composer install from the committed composer.lock on PHP 7.4.33, then vendor/bin/phpunit

new stack, in order, first that succeeds: (1) composer install from the same lock on PHP 8.3; (2) composer update within the project's own constraints; (3) composer install --ignore-platform-reqs; every failed step is a finding, not a fix
both stacks: a failure that names allow-plugins is retried once with --no-plugins
no change to a source or test file, to phpunit.xml.dist or to composer.json; a change that is needed to run is a finding
followUp: rules learned from the misses go in a separate file, follow-up-rules.md, after the score; nothing in rules/ changes between this freeze and the score
